scope: Strict named-flower, two-hand, and contact pre-gate for global frames 254-342
summary: The human-free window preserves two tracked flower identities, but it is rejected because a second independent mechanical hand is not clearly observable and cannot be tracked without identity ambiguity.
evidence: Two real source flower heads track for 89/89 frames; after source-instance restoration, independent candidate tracks also remain nonempty for 89/89 frames with adjacent-IoU means 0.8047 and 0.7839.

The first left-hand retry is empty for 79/89 frames and its dense board shows drift to the pink background ribbon; the independently tracked right gripper is nonempty for 89/89 frames with adjacent-IoU mean 0.9306.

The shifted left-support retry is nonempty for 89/89 frames with adjacent-IoU mean 0.9657 and maximum centroid step 10.07 pixels, but dense review resolves only an occluded palm-root/wrist region rather than a clearly separate articulated second hand; its same-run right hand is empty for 48/89 frames.

A byte-preserving merge of the numerically stable left and right tracks is retained as PARTIAL evidence only; the semantic two-mechanical-hands-visible gate remains false and no contact gate is promoted.
lessons: Low centroid motion and high mask IoU can describe a stable wrist patch or background object; semantic instance review remains mandatory.
Independent single-instance runs may be merged without changing masks, but merging cannot repair a fundamentally unobservable or fused hand.
limitations: The generic source-to-candidate evaluator for the earlier 70-frame postprocessed candidate does not apply to the restored 89-frame artifact.
No strict all-gates-passed report exists for this window.
next_actions: Regenerate frames 254-342 with both palms and articulated fingers spatially separated and simultaneously visible.
Repeat named-flower restoration, two independent hand tracks, contact pairing, and unchanged strict thresholds before considering this window for expansion.
